name: Calendarista Marina Lite – Marina, Berth & Boat Slip Booking
author: typps

sections.description:
Calendarista Marina Lite takes berth bookings for a marina, harbour or boatyard, on its own website. Boaters see your real marina plan, enter their boat’s size, pick a berth it fits and book it. You run arrivals, departures and changes from a front desk inside WordPress.

There is no limit on marinas, berths or bookings, nothing is charged per booking, and every booking and guest stays in your own WordPress database.

Need online payments or seasonal contracts? Get Calendarista Marina.

A marina plan guests can read. Upload the plan you already have (a drawing, an aerial photo or an SVG) and place each berth on it. Guests choose dates and crew, and every berth shows whether it is free, taken or on hold. Filters for shore power, water, pump-out and step-free access narrow the choice, and there is a list view for small screens.

Berths that fit the boat. Give each berth a maximum length, beam and depth. Guests enter their boat’s length, beam and draft, and a berth it will not fit says why and cannot be booked. The check runs again on the server, so it cannot be bypassed. The boat’s name, registration and type are kept on the booking.

Prices per night or per metre. Price a berth type at one price a night, or per metre or foot of boat.

  • Charge the berth’s length when it is longer than the boat, and set a minimum charged length.
  • A surcharge for multihulls, and different rates for longer boats.
  • Seasons, weekend prices and holidays matched night by night, with discounts for longer stays.
  • Work in metres or in feet, marina by marina.
  • Tax included or added on top, and a municipal tourist tax per person per night with child exemptions, a cap on nights and a monthly report.

Real berth inventory. Every night of every berth is a row in its own ledger, so two boats can never be booked onto the same berth for the same night, even in the same second. Adding a berth to a trip holds it for fifteen minutes while the guest checks out.

Book a berth, or a type of berth. Let guests choose their exact berth, or let them book “a mooring buoy” and assign the buoy yourself later. A club or rally can book several berths in one trip.

Extras with real stock. Shore power, car parking, pump-out, kayak hire: priced per stay, per night or per person. Give an item a stock and every booking holds its quantity for each night, so the fourth kayak is never sold.

A front desk. One list of every reservation, from your website or entered by you. Check guests in and out, move a stay to other dates or another berth, record what guests pay at the desk and what you hand back. Close days for the whole marina or for some berths, for maintenance or a private event, and those nights stop being bookable everywhere.

Keep other booking sites in step. Each berth has its own calendar link for any booking site that reads iCal, and you can follow their calendars back, so a night sold elsewhere shows as taken on your map.

Emails you can edit. A confirmation with a calendar file, a cancellation, and a notice to you for every web booking. Change the wording with placeholders and watch a live preview.

Set up in minutes. A setup wizard builds your first marina with priced berth types, berths on a starter map, extras and a draft booking page. A checklist on the Dashboard ticks itself as you go, and “Preview as a guest” shows your map inside your own theme before you publish. Want to look around first? Load the demo marina, a complete sample marina you can remove again in one click.

More than one marina. Run every marina you own from one install, each with its own currency, berths, prices and booking page.

Calendarista Marina

Lite is complete for taking bookings. Calendarista Marina adds what a busier marina needs:

  • Online payments by card through Stripe’s hosted page or with PayPal, with deposits and refunds through the same provider.
  • Seasonal and annual berths: contracts billed monthly, with electricity and water meters.
  • FatturaPA electronic invoices for Italian marinas.
  • The Calendarista companion app for iOS and Android.
  • Direct email support.

Moving up keeps everything: both plugins read the same tables, and Lite steps aside when Calendarista Marina is activated.

External services

This plugin connects to external services only when you set them up.

Calendars you follow under Channels. When you paste another site’s calendar link (from another booking site) under Channels → Follow a calendar, the plugin downloads that calendar from the address you entered about every fifteen minutes, to mark the nights it lists as taken. The request carries your site’s address in its user agent and sends nothing else. Nothing is fetched until you add a calendar, and removing it stops the downloads. The terms and privacy policy of the site that provides the calendar apply.

The confirmation email offers guests an “Add to Google Calendar” link. It is an ordinary link: nothing is sent to Google unless the guest clicks it.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New, or upload the zip, and activate it. WordPress 6.4 or newer and PHP 8.1 or newer are required, with MySQL or MariaDB using InnoDB (standard on almost every host). It also runs on SQLite, as WordPress Playground does.
  2. Open Calendarista Marina Lite in the admin menu. The setup wizard opens the first time.
  3. Name your marina, choose your berth types and prices, and let the wizard create a draft booking page. Publish it when you are happy, or move the block or the [calendarista_marina_map] shortcode to any page you prefer.
  4. Make a test booking on that page and watch it arrive under Reservations.
sections.faq:
Is there a limit on marinas, berths or bookings?

No. Lite takes unlimited bookings, for as many marinas and berths as you run from one install, and never charges per booking.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. The plugin has no dependencies.

Do I have to draw a map?

No. Upload any plan you already have, even a photo of the plan in the harbour office, and drag the berths onto it. Without a plan the berths start in tidy rows, and guests can also book from the list view.

How do guests pay?

On arrival. The booking is confirmed straight away with the full amount due at the desk, where you record it under Reservations.

Where does the guest data live?

In your own WordPress database. There is no external account holding your guest list. The plugin supports WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools.

Can I stop double bookings with another booking site?

Yes. Under Channels, copy each berth’s calendar link into the other site, and follow that site’s calendar link back. They check each other every few hours.

Can staff use it without being administrators?

Yes. Choose which roles can open it under Settings.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing. Deleting the plugin keeps your marinas and bookings, so a reinstall picks up where you left off.

Is it translated?

The plugin is ready for translation, and its translations are made by the community on translate.wordpress.org. WordPress installs them for you in your site’s language as they become available.

Where is the source code for the admin screens and the marina map?

In the plugin itself. The bundles in admin/build and frontend/build are built from the TypeScript sources in admin/src and frontend/src, with the build configuration alongside them (package.json, vite.config.js, vite.frontend.config.js). Run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin folder to rebuild them.

How do I move up to Calendarista Marina?

Install and activate Calendarista Marina. Your marinas, berths, rates, bookings and settings carry over as they are, and Lite steps aside by itself. You can then delete Lite; deleting it never removes data.
